page: Vultr voc-g-2c-8gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the CPU includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The hardware configuration is completed by 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not feature any GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results show a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance reached 3135.87, placing it in the top 10% tier, whereas multi-core performance scored 6213.65, falling into the middle 50% average. Memory bandwidth benchmarks indicate a weak bottom 25% performance for cached small-block reads at 298.13 GB/sec, but large-block reads and writes align with the middle 50% average at 71.86 GB/sec and 53.72 GB/sec respectively. Passmark CPU tests consistently place the instance in the bottom 25% across general, extended instructions, encryption, and physics evaluations.

The instance exhibits notable performance bottlenecks in database and web serving workloads. Passmark database operations scored 1074.47, and static web serving throughput reached 2.26 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 10% tier. Redis SET operations also registered in the bottom 25% at 4.8 million operations per second. For machine learning tasks, text generation with a small 135M model achieved an average speed of 112.52 tokens per second, but performance dropped to a poor 4.47 tokens per second with a medium 7B model. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-core ratio, this instance offers qualitative resource stability for lightweight general-purpose tasks, basic file compression, and low-concurrency application hosting, though it is constrained for intensive database or high-throughput web serving.
description: Vultr voc-g-2c-8gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance powered by a 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC x86_64 processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs (1 physical core, 2 threads) and 8.0 GB of RAM. It features 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and no GPU. Performance benchmarks reveal a top-tier single-core stress-ng score of 3135.87, though multi-core CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth remain average. Significant performance bottlenecks exist in database operations and static web serving, both scoring in the bottom 10% tier. Additionally, Passmark CPU and encryption tests place in the bottom 25%. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic single-threaded tasks, and low-concurrency applications, but it is not suited for high-throughput database hosting or complex large language model inference.
